passage: In the Lindqvist laboratory, researchers measured dehydrogenase activity in a liver homogenate by following production of NADH, which absorbs light at 340 nm with a molar extinction coefficient of 6,220 M⁻¹cm⁻¹, whereas NAD⁺ does not absorb appreciably at this wavelength. The homogenate was diluted 20-fold in assay buffer before use, and 1 mL reactions in a 1 cm cuvette contained saturating substrate and NAD⁺ at 25 °C. Absorbance at 340 nm was recorded every minute. A blank containing all components except substrate was run in parallel to correct for non-enzymatic changes. The initial linear region of the progress curve was used to calculate velocity. The researchers wished to report the activity of the undiluted homogenate and to compare it with a published value from a different laboratory. The spectrophotometer was zeroed against buffer, and all readings fell within the instrument's linear range. All procedures followed the laboratory's standard operating protocols, and raw data were archived before analysis.

questions.stem: What is the change in A340 of the sample between 0 and 2 minutes, according to Table 1?
questions.trap: Using the raw 2-minute reading (0.174), the 3-minute change (0.187) or the per-minute change (0.062) instead of A(2 min) minus A(0 min) = 0.124.

questions.stem: Why is a blank lacking substrate included?

options.A: To detect absorbance changes that occur without the enzyme-catalyzed reaction
options.B: To increase the extinction coefficient of NADH
options.D: To ensure the enzyme is saturated

questions.explanation: The blank accounts for background drift (e.g., contaminating reductants, instrument drift) independent of the reaction under study.
questions.trap: Thinking the blank saturates the enzyme, converts NAD⁺ to NADH or changes the extinction coefficient; its role is to reveal absorbance change without the reaction.

questions.stem: Using Beer–Lambert, what is the initial rate of NADH formation in the cuvette (µM/min), and what activity does the undiluted homogenate have (µM/min)?

options.A: 10 µM/min in the cuvette; 10 µM/min in the undiluted homogenate
options.B: 0.01 µM/min in the cuvette; 0.2 µM/min in the undiluted homogenate
options.C: 10 µM/min in the cuvette; 200 µM/min in the undiluted homogenate
options.D: 200 µM/min in the cuvette; 4000 µM/min in the undiluted homogenate

questions.explanation: Rate = (ΔA/min)/(ε·l) = 0.0622/6220 = 10 µM/min in the cuvette. Multiply by the 20-fold dilution to get 200 µM/min for the undiluted homogenate.
questions.trap: Skipping the 20-fold dilution factor (same value for cuvette and homogenate), or slipping by a power of ten when converting M to µM.

questions.stem: Which statement about this assay is INCORRECT?

options.A: Substrate must be saturating for the rate to approximate Vmax
options.B: Both NAD⁺ and NADH absorb strongly at 340 nm, so the signal reflects total coenzyme
options.C: The initial linear portion of the curve gives the most reliable velocity
options.D: NADH absorbs at 340 nm while NAD⁺ does not

questions.explanation: Only the reduced coenzyme absorbs at 340 nm; that selective absorbance makes the assay possible.
questions.trap: Believing NAD⁺ also absorbs at 340 nm so the signal reflects total coenzyme; only NADH absorbs, so absorbance tracks NADH production.

questions.stem: Which type of assay couples an enzyme of interest to NADH oxidation so that its activity can be monitored at 340 nm?

options.A: An immunoassay using antibodies against the enzyme
options.B: A gel assay using SDS-PAGE mobility
options.C: A radioactive assay using ³²P-labeled ATP
options.D: A coupled assay using lactate dehydrogenase to reduce pyruvate formed by pyruvate kinase

questions.explanation: Pyruvate kinase produces pyruvate; LDH then oxidizes NADH to NAD⁺, causing a decrease in A340 proportional to pyruvate kinase activity.
questions.trap: Choosing assays that do not link activity to NADH absorbance (immunoassay, gel mobility, radiolabel); only the coupled LDH assay changes A340.
